//: Copy to server/api/appsettings.Production.json and fill the CHANGE_ME values. Only 'Identity' is required; every other section has a working default and is optional. The DB connection is injected by docker-compose from the .env POSTGRES_* values — do NOT put ConnectionStrings here.
//SYNC: This is a DOCUMENTED MIRROR of the engine's own src/DevC.KPI.API/appsettings.json (the source of truth for every available section). There is no automatic sync — when the engine adds or renames a setting, this template must be updated by hand. A key here that the engine version you run doesn't know is simply ignored (and vice versa: a new engine setting won't appear here until someone adds it).
//Identity: REQUIRED. OIDC/identity settings. EncryptionKey MUST be a stable random secret (`openssl rand -base64 32`) — changing it invalidates every issued token/cookie. The two URLs are the OIDC issuer + client base; for the one-box stack they are the nginx address (https). Behind the proxy the whole API runs under PathBase=/api, so IdentityBaseUrl ends in /api/. On a real domain, set these (and the client template) to that host and restart.
//Seed: OPTIONAL, first-run only. Leave empty to get the interactive setup wizard on first launch (create the initial admin in the browser). To provision the admin non-interactively (automated installs), set AdminEmail + AdminPassword; IncludeDemoLogin=true also creates the public read-only demo login. Honoured ONLY while the app is uninitialised (no admin yet); ignored afterwards. Can also be supplied as env vars: Seed__AdminEmail / Seed__AdminPassword / Seed__IncludeDemoLogin.
//Reporting: Runtime reporting config. ConfigPath = the folder the engine scans for tenant config (config/<tenant>/); PluginsPaths = where plugin bundles are dropped. Both are set to the container mount points HERE so the engine finds them even if the compose env (Reporting__ConfigPath) is absent — if ConfigPath is empty the engine falls back to a dev path that does not exist in the container, so the mounted config is silently ignored (no datasources, no reports). Relay is only for the on-prem datasource proxy; Reporting:Secrets is an inline fallback for datasource secret values (prefer the Secrets:Path files below). RestartOnPluginChange/PluginChangePollSeconds control plugin hot-reload polling.

Reporting.//ConfigPaths: Extra config roots to scan, in addition to the compose-provided ConfigPath. Usually empty.
Reporting.//Relay: On-prem datasource proxy relay (only if you run the proxy). Url = the relay hub URL; Key = the shared relay key (better set via the KPI_RELAY_KEY / KPI_RELAY_KEY_FILE env var than in this file).
Reporting.//Secrets: Inline datasource secret values, keyed by the name referenced in a datasource YAML. Prefer secret FILES under Secrets:Path (below) or same-named env vars over putting secrets in this file.

//Secrets: Directory of datasource secret files (connection strings, proxy key hashes). Set to the container mount /srv/kpi/secrets so the engine loads them even without the compose SECRETS__PATH env — empty makes it fall back to a dev path absent in the container, so secrets are silently not loaded.
//Email: OPTIONAL SMTP sender for invitation / password-reset mails. Enabled=false means no SMTP mail is sent (invitations must then be shared manually). To use it: Enabled=true and fill From/Host/User/Password/Port/SSL.
//MSGraphMail: OPTIONAL Microsoft Graph mail sender — an alternative to SMTP Email for invitation / password-reset mails via an Azure AD app registration. Enabled=false = off. To use it: Enabled=true and fill From (a mailbox the app may send as) + TenantId / ClientId / ClientSecret from the app registration. Do not enable both Email and MSGraphMail.
//Serilog: OPTIONAL logging levels. Raise Default to "Debug" for troubleshooting; the overrides quiet noisy framework categories. Logs go to the container stdout (docker compose logs api).
//AllowedHosts: Host-header filter. Semicolon-separate multiple names (e.g. "localhost;kpi.example.com"); "*" allows any.
//PathBase: The whole API is mounted under /api behind the proxy; UsePathBase strips it. Leave as /api for the standard nginx setup.
